notes: Verified independently: Target Australia (target.com.au, part of Wesfarmers' Kmart Group) is an unrelated corporate entity from S.N. 22 Target US (target.com, Target Corporation) - separate platform, separate Constructor.io search key (key_kWcXakjuyHSxpu75 vs Target US's PerimeterX-protected redsky API), separate catalogue, no franchise relationship; genuinely independent, not a duplicate-company case. robots.txt returns Akamai edge 'Access Denied' (not a Claude-specific Disallow rule - it's a generic bot-manager block applying to all direct/naive requests including plain robots.txt fetch), so this is a WAF-bypass situation, not a Rule-3 opt-out. Access: home page (/) loads directly via curl_cffi with most desktop Chrome/Edge profiles, but individual /c/ category pages return Akamai 403 for those same profiles - curl_cffi impersonate=safari17_2_ios and chrome99_android got through cleanly (200, full HTML) on category pages; other profiles (safari17_0/safari15_5/firefox) returned a 2.6KB bot-check interstitial. Scoped strictly to Home department navigation (/c/home/W99700, 19 sub-departments, 5376 products) per brief - did not enumerate the whole site (fashion, toys, electronics, etc. out of scope by construction, never touched). Counts verified via Constructor.io's browse API (ac.cnstrc.com/browse/group_id/<ID>?key=key_kWcXakjuyHSxpu75), whose total_num_results is embedded in every category page's own HTML as data-cnstrc-num-results (cross-checked match on Home Decor: both report 628) - this is the exact number the site's own PLP uses to drive Constructor's search-analytics beacon, not a raw Shopify/Magento-style inflated catalogue total. Exhaustion-verified on two nodes of different size: Photo Frames (page through num_results_per_page=50, page 3 returns the final 17, page 4 returns 0, 117 unique product IDs collected across all pages) and Drinkware (page through num_results_per_page=30, page 3 returns the final 5, 65 unique IDs collected) - both matched the reported total exactly, so Constructor's total_num_results is trusted for the remaining un-exhausted nodes. Traversed all 19 top-level Home sub-departments (Appliances, Art & Craft, Bathroom, Bedroom, Dining, DIY, Furniture, Gym & Fitness, Home Decor, Home Office, Kitchen, Laundry, Lighting, Outdoor Living, Party/Cards/Wrap, Pets, Storage, Travel, Winter Warmth) via the cnstrc browse tree to find every decor-relevant leaf, not just the 'Home Decor' node, per Rule 0 (e.g. Lighting and the Dining tableware/glassware leaves are separate top-level departments from 'Home Decor' and were pulled in). EXCLUDED after title inspection: Home Decor's Cushions/Blankets & Throws (textiles), Candles & Home Fragrance (140 items, sampled titles all scented candles/reed diffusers - home fragrance), Mats & Rugs (textiles), Essential Oils (home fragrance). Lighting's Globes (22 items, sampled titles all Mirabella E27/E14/B22 LED/GLS bulbs - Australian English 'globe' = light bulb, explicitly excluded). Dining's Cutlery (cutlery excluded) and Napery (table linens, textiles). Entire Bathroom (477), Kitchen (687), Art & Craft (445), Storage (369), Bedroom (658), Outdoor Living (88), Appliances, DIY, Furniture, Gym & Fitness, Home Office, Laundry, Party/Cards/Wrap, Pets, Travel, Winter Warmth departments excluded as furniture/storage/fixtures/plumbing/textiles/consumables/craft-supplies/hardware, confirmed by title sample of Bathroom Accessories (dominated by toilet brushes/soap dispensers/bins - functional, only 2/15 sampled were decor trays), Food & Drinks under Kitchen (confectionery), and Artistry under Art & Craft (paint/craft supplies, not finished wall art). MIXED ROLL-UPS DROPPED PER 'drop, don't pad' RULE (site reports one qty for the whole node but title sampling showed real contamination by out-of-scope product types, and Constructor exposes no product-type facet on any of these nodes to isolate an exact in-scope subset - only newarrivals/colour/price/brand/delivery/material facets are available site-wide): Home Decor > Pots & Plants (104, sampled 15 titles: ~80% 'Artificial ___' faux plants explicitly excluded, only 3/15 were genuine pots/planters); Home Decor > Decor Accessories (76, sampled 30 titles: ~27% out-of-scope furniture/storage/faux-flower items - coat stands x2, floating shelves x2, magazine file, jewellery box, artificial flowers/garland - mixed with genuine trays/bowls/candle holders); Home Decor > Wall Art (11, full list inspected exhaustively: only 7/11 are genuine framed canvas/art prints, the other 4 are window film x2, dimensional craft paint, and a kids' 'memory frame' craft product); Home Decor > Outdoor Decor (3, full list: 1 duplicate string-lights item already counted under Lighting, 1 genuine decor item (pebbles), 1 window film - net too small and contaminated to be a clean node); Bathroom > Bathroom Accessories (90, dominated by functional/plumbing items per above). KEPT despite being under the same 'Home Decor' node because sample inspection showed them clean or the brief explicitly names the product type as always in-scope: Clocks (3, incl. one digital weather station sold alongside the 2 decorative clocks - kept, brief says 'Clocks (all types)'), Vases (20, all genuine ceramic/glass vases), Mirrors (31, all genuine mirror types including travel/handheld - Rule 0.3 'ALL mirrors in scope'), Photo Frames (117, exhaustively sampled/paged, all genuine picture frames), Draught & Door Stoppers (5, small whimsical decorative door-stop/draught-stopper items, all 5 titles genuinely decorative novelty objects, not structural hardware). Dining department's Dinnerware/Drinkware/Servingware filed under 'Kitchen & Dining' per brief naming convention (matches S.N. 22 Target US precedent) even though Target AU's own site names the department 'Dining' (separate from its 'Kitchen' department, which is 100% excluded as cookware/appliances/food-storage). No Rule 0.6 type-tree/room-tree overlap found - Target AU's Home department uses a single flat type-based taxonomy (departments like Bathroom/Bedroom/Dining/Lighting are product-type groupings, not a duplicated room-based re-cut of the same items).
